claims.text: A 10-year-old girl presented with hematochezia, tenesmus and abdominal pain. Workup showed elevated fecal calprotectin of 2030 μg/g, biopsy findings of chronic inflammation, and a 6-cm segment of terminal ileal inflammation with mild rectal involvement on computed tomography enterography. She was diagnosed with Crohn's disease (Paris A1b, L3, L4a, B1, G0) and started on adalimumab.

claims.text: The first IV loading dose of ustekinumab 260 mg was followed by a transient erythematous infusion-site rash, and one SQ injection was tolerated 8 weeks later. After 4 months without ustekinumab because of insurance gaps, a one-time 260 mg IV re-induction was begun at an outside hospital; within 30 s she developed acute respiratory distress with facial cyanosis and dyspnea. The infusion was discontinued, intramuscular epinephrine, oxygen and fluids were given, and symptoms completely resolved with observation.
